summary.headline: Axiscades Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 20% YoY to ₹359.1 crore, but reported EBITDA of ₹11.4 crore was hit by ₹58.3 crore one-time write-offs and ESOP costs.
summary.overview: Consolidated Q2 FY27 revenue was ₹359.1 crore, up 20% YoY and 3.6% QoQ, with retained business revenue of ₹195.6 crore up 30% YoY. Phase one of the divestment closed on 30 September 2026, while phase two (aerospace engineering services, guaranteed consideration plus earn-out) has slipped from November to February 2027. Reported profit after tax was ₹47.3 crore, driven by a ₹129.3 crore pre-tax exceptional gain on discontinued operations, offset by continuing-operations losses from impairments of ₹38.4 crore. Management guided to a recovery from Q3 with corporate costs, ESOP and transaction costs falling, and targeted ~20% post-ESOP EBITDA margins for defence, ZEDA and aerospace.

segments.name: Defence (DRDO, PSU, MoD)
segments.commentary: Defence cited as delivering H1 revenue of ₹222.7 crore, up 46%, at a 17.6% margin; the DRDO/PSU/defence business together generated ₹29 crore EBITDA at 23% margin in Q2 before ESOP.

segments.name: ZEDA
segments.commentary: H1 revenue grew 55% to ₹97.9 crore at a 27.6% margin, driven by ~47% on new customer wins; management targets triple-digit growth in Q3 and ~20% EBITDA margin, with an IPSG acquisition announced.

segments.name: Aerospace
segments.commentary: H1 revenue of ₹23.1 crore; CloudWave (acquired, consolidated from 10 Sept) contributed from its first quarter. Full quarterly contribution expected in Q3 and Q4.

segments.name: Corporate / ACTL and ADT Solutions
segments.commentary: Listed parent corporate cost ~₹15 crore a quarter with revenue yet to scale; ADT Solutions in solvent liquidation. ESOP, corporate cost and ADT EBITDA loss together total ~₹31 crore in Q2, ~16% of retained revenue.

guidance_outlook: Q3 FY27 core revenue (defence, ZEDA, aerospace, space) targeted at least 30% growth over Q2, with a 45% upper band; management guided to ~285-300 crore total revenue in Q3 and ~375-405 crore in Q4 (approximate, subject to supply chain).
Management aims for ~15-16% post-ESOP EBITDA margin in Q3 and ~20% (plus or minus 1%) in Q4 FY27; ESOP charge to fall to a single-digit percentage of EBITDA by Q4.
Corporate overheads to reduce to ~₹12 crore a quarter; ESOP charge ~₹6 crore a quarter; legal and functional charges to normalise to ~₹4-5 crore a quarter from ₹14.5 crore in Q2.

Phase two divestment (aerospace engineering services, valued at US$206 million) expected to close by February 2027, delayed from November 2026 due to regulatory approvals for new company formation; expected to add ~₹1,100 crore extraordinary gain in Q4 FY27, with ~₹20 crore further transaction costs.

Guaranteed consideration schedule: ₹121 crore received in October, ₹32 crore in November, ~₹504 crore in February 2027, ₹56 crore in July 2027 and ₹682 crore in December 2028; earn-out (~₹550 crore) based on FY28 EBITDA, not FY27.

Management said FY27 revenue aspiration of ₹1,350 crore (set before divestment) no longer holds; rebuilding to ₹1,000+ crore on the retained base plus acquisitions, with FY28 base revenue as the benchmark.
Executable orders of about ₹1,000 crore; ~₹379 crore executed to date and ₹600-720 crore expected to execute over the next two quarters, subject to supply chain delays.

Planned acquisitions: about four lined up, with two or three targeted to close in Q4 FY27; each expected to contribute ₹600-750 crore at full scale, subject to due diligence and ITAR/CFIUS-type regulatory timelines.
Space expected to become revenue-generating in FY28 and EBITDA positive thereafter.
capex_capacity: Acquired ~8 acres of land in Telangana for MAC (missile and missile subsystems complex); construction to commence at appropriate stage; full functionality may take 1-1.5 years, plus ~6 months for certification; interim operations at Bangalore facility.
Shifted ~500 people to a new facility (Devanahalli Aero Lab), which raised other costs (conveyance, canteen); transport cost per employee cut from ₹27,000 to ₹22,000.
Building manufacturing infrastructure and skilled manpower to pivot from services to manufacturing-led model; ZEDA supply chain being strengthened, with component lead times of 12-18 months.
Development orders for missile electronics, electrical, mechanical and system integration progressing at Bangalore; production to follow at appropriate time.
Employee cost guided at roughly ₹48-54 crore a quarter for the next two quarters, not increasing.
demand_pricing: Defence: assured forecast visibility of ~₹5,000 crore (up from ~₹4,500 crore previously), including ~₹80 crore of design orders; management says AFP is used only for the defence context.
Q3 defence revenue targeted at ~₹120 crore from DRDO and ~₹45 crore from direct MoD business; Q4 ~₹150 crore DRDO and ~₹60 crore MoD (supply-chain dependent).
ZEDA targeted ~₹81 crore in Q3 and ₹90-105 crore in Q4; aerospace ~₹51 crore in Q3 and ~₹75 crore in Q4.

ZEDA pillars: embedded boards with LLM/SLM layers, humanoid/robotics (first order from a US company, Humanoid), data-centre chillers (Google as customer), and semiconductor equipment (Applied Materials as customer).
Supply chain constraints in strategic electronics, PCBs and components (12-18 month lead times) may delay deliveries; some premium cost may be paid, impacting margin by ~2%.

qa_highlights.question: What quarterly growth and margin trajectory should be expected for Q3 and Q4 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets at least 30% QoQ growth in core verticals in Q3 (up to ~45%), ~15-16% post-ESOP EBITDA margin in Q3 and ~20% in Q4, with ESOP falling to under ~8% of EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Is the remaining ₹1,200 crore-plus of divestment gain on track, and what transaction costs follow?
qa_highlights.answer: Phase two (US$206 million, aerospace engineering services) targeted to close by February 2027, generating ~₹1,100 crore gain in Q4; ~₹35 crore transaction costs incurred so far and ~₹20 crore more expected.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the revenue target change, and is the FY27 revenue outlook being withdrawn?
qa_highlights.answer: Management denied withdrawing targets; said the ₹1,350 crore aspiration pre-dated the divestment, which removed ~60% of revenue from a ₹514 crore base; FY27 execution of ₹600-720 crore is expected over the next two quarters on top of ₹379 crore already executed.

qa_highlights.question: Why did phase two margin fall, and how is debt funded if deals slip?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said 72% of consideration is guaranteed (₹1,686 crore of ₹2,275 crore); Q2 decline attributed to salary increments, planned Airbus shutdown and ₹3.7 crore ECL charge; net debt of ~₹525-556 crore mainly from CloudWave acquisition, with ₹85 crore repaid in October.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan for ZEDA, including fundraising and acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: ZEDA's four pillars are embedded boards, humanoids, data-centre chillers and semiconductor equipment; acquisitions could more than double its FY26 revenue of ~₹125 crore; a standalone fundraise is under NDA and undisclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Can H2 revenue guidance be broken down, and does it include acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H2 guidance is based on the current order book, excluding future acquisitions; Q3 revenue ₹285-300 crore and Q4 ₹375-405 crore, split across DRDO, MoD, ZEDA and aerospace.

risks_watch: Phase two divestment (aerospace engineering services, US$206 million) has slipped from November 2026 to February 2027; closing drives the ~₹1,100 crore Q4 gain and ~₹550 crore earn-out, so timing and new-company regulatory approvals are key to monitor.

Q3 and Q4 FY27 margin path: management targets ~15-16% post-ESOP EBITDA in Q3 and ~20% in Q4 (plus or minus 1%), against 11.4 crore reported EBITDA in Q2; ESOP charge (~₹6 crore a quarter target) and corporate overhead reduction to ~₹12 crore a quarter must materialise.

Supply chain: 12-18 month lead times for strategic electronics, PCBs and components could delay deliveries and add premium costs of roughly 2% margin impact; ₹600-720 crore execution over two quarters is conditional on this.

FY27 revenue: management says the ₹1,350 crore aspiration pre-dated the divestment and is no longer the benchmark; rebuilding to ₹1,000+ crore on the retained base plus acquisitions, with 2-3 acquisitions targeted for Q4 and each expected to add ₹600-750 crore at full scale, subject to ITAR/CFIUS-type timelines.

Balance sheet: gross borrowings ₹624 crore and net debt ₹556 crore at 30 Sept 2026 (₹200 crore relates to CloudWave); ₹85 crore repaid in October; the company also flagged a standalone ZEDA fundraise under NDA, with details undisclosed.
key_quotes: Phase two is classified as held for sale and is scheduled for closure in February or earlier.
We are 100 percent confident about it because the buyer is far far more ego in terms of making this happen.
We are not withdrawing or silently dropping anything and on we don't do that okay.
The ESOP charge took about half of our EBITDA. That is the highest it will be.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the strategic direction, defence visibility and phase two closing ("100 percent confident"), but noticeably cautious and hedged on quarterly numbers, using "approximate", "band" and "not a guidance" language. Evasive on the ZEDA fundraise, acquisition targets and the EBITDA impact of supply-chain premiums, which were not quantified.
